![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14238118/assets/bc3809e55e601738d56be6885475ed442dec1fb3a0d2e19da14be045510f73dc.png)

The above scatter plot shows the relationship between age and years of experience of a group of professional soccer players. 

Given that none of the points overlap, which of the following statements are true?

I. Only one player has exactly $10$ years of experience.

II. There are two players aged $21.$

III. None of the players has fewer than $6$ years of experience.
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine our scatter plot.

- Statement I is true. The scatter plot has only one dot whose vertical coordinate equals $10,$ namely, $(21,10).$ This means only one of the players has exactly $10$ years of experience.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14238118/assets/209759f5d70fd8587740d1da840f9da838a3c9a055a0d1e962f76c1cd6341fd3.png)

- Statement II is true. The scatter plot has two dots whose horizontal coordinate equals $21,$ namely, $(21,10)$ and $(21,12).$ This means that two players are $21$ years old.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14238118/assets/753c503d6751363b1c7d2dc449f1c5f11baec159b1e938e8c807938512111750.png)

- Statement III is false. From the scatter plot, one player has fewer than $6$ years of experience. The dot below the horizontal line represents this player.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14238118/assets/66facd1a0683f420aa2ac3d7bfd54290bdb009850bc66cc7523ee569ec81daea.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
